summary: Human-vote leaderboards and an API that routes work to the top-ranked model.
editor_note: Model routing gets more credible when taste is measured by people, not inferred from synthetic scores. Intelligence turns millions of side-by-side Design Arena votes into format-specific leaderboards, then exposes a gateway that selects the top-ranked model. Unlike a static benchmark, the product links live human preference data to an OpenAI-compatible API. The risk is identity and metric drift: public surfaces still reference Arcada domains and disagree on user totals.

product_evidence.claim: The official site exposes live leaderboards across code, image, video, audio, slides, SVG, and other formats, with Elo-rating and win-rate views built from human comparisons.
The Gateway API accepts standard message payloads and input/output formats, then selects the top-ranked Design Arena model without requiring the caller to specify a model.
TechCrunch reports that Design Arena serves millions of users and supplies human evaluations to frontier labs, turning participation into a continuously refreshed preference dataset.

market_context.primary_user: AI labs, application developers, and model buyers comparing or routing across generative models for specific output formats.
market_context.differentiation: Intelligence connects side-by-side human preference data to a model-selection gateway instead of treating a static benchmark as the end product.
market_context.why_now: Rapid model turnover and inconsistent quality across modalities make continuously refreshed human evaluation more useful than one universal score.

risks.claim: The falsifiable risk is whether the company can reconcile Arcada-era domains and conflicting user metrics while keeping human votes resistant to bias, gaming, and sampling drift.
risks.basis: VentureDex editorial assessment from official product surfaces, API documentation, and the Seed report.
